inicio.titulo: Foundations: how agents use a website today, and what your site shows them
inicio.lead: Reading, operating the screen, and calling a tool: the three ways an agent can use your site. You see the accessibility tree it receives, fix your HTML, place MCP and WebMCP, read the draft's status with its date, and leave with a diagnosis of your site. All local, no quota spent.
inicio.capa_alt: Dark monitor with a browser open on a form and a cable plugged into a connector beside it.

numeros.t: scripts in the kit, all local

inicio.aulas_sub: From what the agent does today to your site's plan: three ways, the tree, the HTML, MCP and WebMCP, stable vs. draft, who shows up, the diagnosis, and the plan.

itens: Web devs, makers, or technical site owners who edit HTML and JavaScript and run commands in the terminal.
People who want AI agents to use their site, in the browser and through MCP, and have never worked on this.
People who have heard of WebMCP and want to know what is stable and what is still a draft.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Run the three ways an agent can use a site against your page and see which one works.
Read the accessibility tree the agent receives and bring the HTML problems down to zero.
Say, with a date and a source, where WebMCP and the browsers' positions stand.
Run WebMCP Readiness on your machine and build your site's plan for agents.

blocos.t: Where this course fits in the WebMCP Program
itens: This is course 0: the foundation for the other five. Suggested order: 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5.
After it: 1 · MCP server for your service, 2 · WebMCP on the page, 3 · browser agents, 4 · security, 5 · expert.
Before you start: Node 20 or newer, git, and Python 3. Linux or macOS; on Windows, use WSL.
